model_annotation:
This plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) of several methods as a function of co-occurrence number. The x-axis represents "Co-occurrence Number" on a logarithmic scale, ranging from approximately 3 to about 5,000, with tick marks at 10⁰·⁵ (approximately 3), 10¹, 10¹·⁵ (approximately 30), 10², 10²·⁵ (approximately 300), 10³, and beyond. The y-axis represents "ACC (%)" on a linear scale, ranging from approximately 37% to 65%, with tick marks at intervals of roughly 5 percentage points (40, 45, 50, 55, 60, 65).

Six lines are shown, each corresponding to a different method. The "Base" line (black with circle markers, solid) starts at approximately 38% at the lowest co-occurrence number and rises gradually to approximately 43.5% at the highest, showing a relatively flat trend. The "FT" line (light blue with downward-triangle markers, solid) begins at approximately 39.5% and increases to approximately 47.5%. The "IKE" line (red/salmon with upward-triangle markers, solid) starts at approximately 43% and rises to approximately 49.5%. The "MEND" line (brown/mauve with diamond markers, solid) begins at approximately 44.5% and increases to approximately 56.5%, showing a steady upward trend. The "MEMIT" line (purple with circle markers, solid) starts at approximately 43.5% and rises to approximately 54.5%. The "ROME" line (green with square markers, solid) begins at approximately 51% and increases to approximately 65.5%, maintaining the highest values across all co-occurrence numbers. All lines exhibit a generally increasing trend as co-occurrence number grows, with ROME consistently occupying the highest position and Base the lowest throughout the range.
